main.claim: Open Dictation, click the microphone, allow access, and talk: your words appear as text you can edit. It works best in Chrome, Edge or Safari. Say comma, period or new line in English, then copy the text or download it as a .txt file.

sections.heading: How to dictate in your browser
sections.body:
Dictation turns your speech into text inside the browser tab. You do not install anything. You open the page, tap the microphone, and speak. The words show up in the text box as you say them.

1. Open [Dictation](https://dictation.lazur.app/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari.
2. Choose your language from the list.
3. Click the microphone and allow access when the browser asks.
4. Speak in full sentences at a normal pace.
5. Click the microphone again to stop, then fix any words the tool got wrong.

**The text is editable.** You can click anywhere in the box, change a word, and keep talking. Watch the first few sentences closely, because that tells you whether the microphone and the language are right.

If the page does not seem to hear you at all, check three things: the microphone you want is selected in your computer's sound settings, the browser has permission to use the microphone, and no other app is recording audio at the same time. Fix one of those, then click the microphone again and speak a full sentence to test it.

sections.heading: What you can do with the text
sections.body:
When you are done, copy all of the text in one click, or download it as a .txt file that opens in any editor. The tool also shows a word count, so you can see how long a draft is while you speak. Use the clear option to start over with an empty box.

Spoken punctuation works in English. Say comma, period, question mark or new line, and the tool writes the mark instead of the word. Other languages still turn your speech into text, but check the marks and add them by hand if they are missing.

sections.heading: Which browser to use
sections.body:
Chrome, Edge and Safari work best, because they include the speech recognition this tool relies on. If the microphone button does nothing, try one of those browsers and check that it can use your microphone. The browser settings for the microphone are the first place to look when a page cannot hear you.

If you are not sure which browser you have, open the page in Chrome or Edge, which are both on the list of browsers that work best.

sections.heading: Where your voice goes
sections.body: Chrome may send the audio you speak to Google's speech service so it can turn the sound into text. That happens in the browser, not on a Lazur server. Lazur does not receive that audio. If you dictate private material, read the privacy section of your browser before you start, and choose a browser or device that fits what you are willing to share.

pages.title: Online Dictation to Text: Talk and Watch It Type | Lazur
pages.description: Turn speech into text online. Click the mic, talk, and watch your words appear in the browser. Edit, copy, or download the text as a .txt file.
pages.claim: Click the microphone in Dictation, allow access, and talk. Your words appear as text you can edit, and you can copy the text or download it as a .txt file. It works in Chrome, Edge or Safari.

sections.heading: How to turn speech into text online
sections.body:
You do not need to type to write a draft. Open the dictation page, tap the microphone, and speak. The browser listens, and the tool shows each word in the text box as it hears it.

1. Open [online dictation](https://dictation.lazur.app/text) in Chrome, Edge or Safari.
2. Choose your language from the list.
3. Click the microphone and allow access when the browser asks.
4. Speak in short sentences, with a small pause at the end of each one.
5. Click the microphone again to stop.

**Pause between sentences.** Recognition is most accurate when you finish a sentence before you start the next one. A run-on sentence often comes out as one long block with the wrong words.

sections.heading: Fix the text and keep going
sections.body:
The text box is editable while you dictate. Click on a word, type the fix, and then continue speaking from where you left off. You do not have to restart the whole draft when one word is wrong.

Say the punctuation as you go. In English, comma, period, question mark and new line all turn into marks and breaks. Read the first paragraph back once you have the rhythm, so the tool and you agree on how it hears your sentences.

For longer drafts, dictate one section at a time. Stop, read it through, then start the next part. A short check after each section catches errors while they are still easy to fix.

sections.heading: Get the text out
sections.body:
When the draft is ready, use the copy button to put all of the text on your clipboard, then paste it into an email, a document or a form. Or download the text as a .txt file, which opens in any text editor.

The word count shows how long the draft is as you speak. Use it to check a length limit, such as a short post or a paragraph for school. Clear the box when you want to start a new draft with an empty page.

sections.heading: Which browser and what to check
sections.body:
Chrome, Edge and Safari work best. If the microphone does not respond, the browser may not have permission to use the mic, or another app may be holding it. Allow the microphone for the site in your browser settings, close other apps that record audio, and try again.

If the words come out wrong for a whole session, check that the right microphone is selected in your computer's sound settings. A headset with a clear mic often gives better results than a laptop mic across the room.

sections.heading: Where your voice goes
sections.body: Chrome may send the audio to Google's speech service to turn it into text. Lazur does not receive that audio. Your text stays in the tab until you copy or download it. Before you dictate anything private, read how your browser handles speech recognition, and decide what you are comfortable sending.

faq.q: Can I dictate online to text?
faq.a: Yes. Open the dictation page, allow the microphone, and speak. Your words appear as text in the box, and you can edit them. When you are finished, copy the text or download it as a .txt file.

faq.q: Is there a free app that turns voice into text?
faq.a: This tool runs in the browser, so you do not install an app. Open the page in Chrome, Edge or Safari and use the microphone. Lazur is a separate Mac app for typing with your voice in other apps.

faq.q: Why does my speech show the wrong words?
faq.a: Speak clearly at a normal pace, use a closer microphone, and pause between sentences. Fix the words you see in the box and keep going. If the problem continues, check the language you picked and the microphone in your sound settings.

pages.title: Online Dictation for Kids: Speak and See the Words | Lazur
pages.description: Let a child speak a sentence and see it turn into text in the browser. Simple steps for a grown-up to set up, plus privacy notes before you start.
pages.claim: A child can tap the microphone, say a sentence, and see the words appear as text they can edit. The tool has no lessons or spelling games, so a grown-up should sit with them and check the result.

sections.heading: How a child can use it
sections.body:
Dictation is a tool for speech, so it works best when a child already knows what they want to say. It shows the words the child speaks, which can help a child see how their speech looks written down.

1. Open [dictation for kids](https://dictation.lazur.app/kids) in Chrome, Edge or Safari on a computer that a grown-up has checked.
2. Choose the language your child speaks.
3. Click the microphone and allow access, with a grown-up there to answer the prompt.
4. Ask the child to say one short sentence, such as the name of their pet or what they had for lunch.
5. Read the text together, then fix any words the tool got wrong.

**Keep sentences short.** Children often speak fast and run their words together. A sentence of six to ten words is easier for the tool to follow, and easier for the child to check.

sections.heading: What the tool does and does not do
sections.body:
Dictation turns speech into text. It does not read words aloud, give spelling lessons, show pictures, or check whether an answer is right. It does not have games or levels, and it does not track progress.

What it does do is useful for a few things. The child can say a sentence and see it written. The grown-up can copy the text, download it as a .txt file, and keep it. The word count shows how long a sentence or story is. Spoken punctuation works in English, so a child can say period or question mark and see the mark appear.

If you want a spelling or reading lesson, use a lesson made for that. This tool is for speaking and reading back what was said.

sections.heading: Check the text together
sections.body:
The tool writes what it hears, and that is not always what the child meant. Read the text out loud with the child, and ask them to point at each word. If a word is wrong, the child can fix it in the box, which is a good chance to talk about how the word is spelled.

Take turns. An adult can say a sentence and the child can check the text. That makes the tool a way to talk about writing, not a test the child has to pass.

sections.heading: Privacy before a child uses it
sections.body:
Chrome may send the audio a child speaks to Google's speech service so that it can turn the sound into text. Lazur does not receive that audio. Before a child uses the tool, a grown-up should know what the browser does with speech and decide whether that fits their family's rules.

Use the computer in a shared room, not a private one, and keep an eye on what is typed. Close the tab when the session is over, and download or copy any text the child wants to keep.

faq.q: Is online dictation safe for kids?
faq.a: It depends on your family's rules. Chrome may send the speech a child says to Google's speech service to turn it into text. Lazur does not receive that audio. Use the tool in a shared room and read your browser's privacy notes before a child starts.

faq.q: Can kids use dictation to practice spelling?
faq.a: Not by itself. The tool turns speech into text, but it does not check spelling or give lessons. A child can say a word, read the text, and fix it with a grown-up. That practice helps only if an adult talks through each word.

faq.q: How does a child start dictation?
faq.a: Open the page in Chrome, Edge or Safari, choose the language, click the microphone, and allow access. Then speak one short sentence. The words appear as text the child can read and edit.

pages.title: Online Dictation in English: Talk and Get Text | Lazur
pages.description: Dictate in English online. Speak, and your words appear as editable text in the browser. Say comma, period or new line, then copy or download the text.
pages.claim: Choose English, click the microphone, and talk. Your words appear as editable text, and spoken punctuation works in English: say comma, period, question mark or new line. Copy the text or download it as a .txt file.

sections.heading: How to dictate in English
sections.body:
English is the language where the spoken punctuation works, so it is the best place to start if you write in English. Choose English from the language list, then use the microphone like this.

1. Open [online dictation in English](https://dictation.lazur.app/english) in Chrome, Edge or Safari.
2. Choose English from the language list.
3. Click the microphone and allow access when the browser asks.
4. Speak one sentence at a time and pause at the end of each.
5. Say the punctuation out loud, then click the microphone again to stop.

**Say the mark, not the symbol.** Say period to get a full stop, question mark for a question, and new line to start a new line. The tool writes the mark when it hears the word.

sections.heading: Spoken punctuation in English
sections.body:
The tool understands the words comma, period, question mark and new line. Say them where you want the mark to go. A sentence such as I will call you tomorrow period is written as I will call you tomorrow with a full stop after it.

Punctuation words can also appear in normal speech. If you say the word period in a sentence about a time of day, the tool may write a full stop instead. Read the text back after each paragraph and fix any mark that landed in the wrong place.

sections.heading: When the English text is wrong
sections.body:
The most common problems are background noise, a mic that is too far away, and fast speech. Move closer to the microphone, speak at a normal pace, and close any app that records sound. A headset usually gives cleaner text than a laptop mic.

Check the language setting too. If the tool is set to another language, English words come out as the nearest match in that language. Choose English again and dictate the first sentence to see whether the text now matches what you said.

If you switch between English and another language in the same session, check the language list before each new draft. A draft that starts in the wrong language is hard to fix word by word, so it is faster to clear the box and begin again with the right setting.

sections.heading: Copy, download and privacy
sections.body:
When the English draft is ready, copy all of the text and paste it into your email or document. The word count helps when a school or work task asks for a set length. You can also download the text as a .txt file.

Chrome may send your speech to Google's speech service to recognize it. Lazur does not receive that audio. The text stays in the tab until you copy or download it.

faq.q: Can I dictate online in English?
faq.a: Yes. Choose English from the language list, allow the microphone, and speak. Your words appear as editable text in the browser. Spoken punctuation like comma, period and new line works in English.

faq.q: How do I add punctuation when I dictate?
faq.a: Say the mark as a word: comma, period or question mark. Say new line or new paragraph to break the text. The tool writes the mark where you said it, so read the text back to check each one.

faq.q: Why are my English words wrong?
faq.a: Check that English is selected, move closer to the microphone, and speak at a normal pace with pauses between sentences. Close other apps that record sound. Then fix the words in the box and keep going.

sections.heading: How to dictate in Hindi
sections.body:
The tool supports many languages, and you choose yours from the list before you start. Open the list, look for Hindi, and select it. If Hindi is not in the list, the tool cannot dictate it, so try another browser or check the language list again.

1. Open [online dictation in Hindi](https://dictation.lazur.app/hindi) in Chrome, Edge or Safari.
2. Choose Hindi from the language list.
3. Click the microphone and allow access when the browser asks.
4. Speak in short sentences at a normal pace.
5. Click the microphone again to stop, then correct the text in the box.

**Choose the language before you speak.** If you switch languages in the middle of a sentence, the words can come out wrong.

sections.heading: Marks and punctuation
sections.body:
The spoken punctuation commands work in English, so words like comma and period do not turn into Hindi marks. Type the marks you need into the text box by hand, including the full stop used in Hindi writing. Read the text back to check where each mark belongs.

A short pause after each sentence helps the tool find the end of the sentence, even when you type the mark yourself later.

When you dictate a longer text, such as a letter or a short essay, break it into paragraphs as you go. Pause, then say new paragraph in English, or press Enter in the box where you want the break. Read each paragraph back before you start the next one, so that a mistake does not carry through the rest of the draft.

The word count is useful for Hindi too. Use it to check the length of a paragraph or a message against the limit you have been given.

sections.heading: When the Hindi text is wrong
sections.body:
Speak clearly and close to the microphone. Background noise, a fan, or a second voice in the room can make the text come out as a mix of words. Use a headset if you have one, and close other apps that use the mic.

If the text is consistently wrong, make sure the browser can use the microphone you want. Then check the language setting again, because a wrong language choice turns speech into the closest match in that language.

sections.heading: Copy the text and check privacy
sections.body:
When the draft is ready, copy all of the text and paste it into a document or message. You can also download it as a .txt file, which opens in any editor that handles Hindi text.

Chrome may send your speech to Google's speech service so it can recognize the words. Lazur does not receive that audio. Read the privacy notes for your browser before you dictate anything private.

faq.q: Can I dictate in Hindi online?
faq.a: Yes, if Hindi is in the tool's language list. Choose Hindi, allow the microphone, and speak. Your words appear as editable text. Check the text, add any marks by hand, then copy it or download it as a .txt file.

faq.q: Does the tool add Hindi punctuation for me?
faq.a: The spoken punctuation commands work in English. For Hindi, type the marks you need, such as the full stop, into the text box after you dictate. Pause between sentences to make the breaks clear.

faq.q: Why does my Hindi come out wrong?
faq.a: Check that Hindi is selected, speak clearly close to the microphone, and reduce background noise. Choosing the wrong language makes the tool guess from the nearest language, so confirm the setting first.

pages.title: Does Microsoft Word Have Dictation? Yes, Here Is How | Lazur
pages.description: Yes, Word has Dictate for Microsoft 365 subscribers. Here is what Microsoft says you need, and how to write text by voice in any browser tab instead.
pages.claim: Yes. Microsoft Word has a Dictate feature for Microsoft 365 subscribers, and it needs a microphone and a reliable internet connection. If you do not have it, Dictation in the browser turns your speech into text you can copy into Word.

sections.heading: Where Dictate is in Word
sections.body:
Microsoft says Dictate turns speech into text in Word, and that it is available to people signed in to Microsoft 365 with a subscription. Word for the web has the steps written out in Microsoft's support article.

1. Open a new or existing document in Word for the web.
2. Go to the Home tab.
3. Select the Dictate button.
4. Wait for the button to show that it is listening, then start speaking.
5. Select Dictate again when you are finished.

Microsoft's article on [dictating in Word for the web](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/dictate-your-documents-in-word-for-the-web) also covers the language choice. Microsoft's article on [Dictate in Microsoft 365](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/dictate-in-microsoft-365) covers the desktop versions for Windows and Mac.

sections.heading: What you need for Dictate
sections.body:
Microsoft lists three needs: a subscription, a device with a working microphone, and a reliable internet connection. Dictate is for subscribers, so if Word shows no Dictate button, check that you are signed in with a Microsoft 365 account that includes it.

The article notes that features can differ between the web, the desktop and the phone apps. If the button is missing in one version, try the same document in another version of Word.

In the web version, the language follows your document by default. To change it, select the gear icon and choose a language from the Spoken Language list. Microsoft also says the service does not store your audio data or transcribed text.

sections.heading: If you do not have Microsoft 365
sections.body:
You can still write by voice without a Word subscription. Open [Dictation](https://dictation.lazur.app/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari, click the microphone, and speak. The words appear as editable text in the browser tab.

When the draft is ready, click copy to put all of the text on your clipboard, then paste it into Word. You can also download the text as a .txt file and open it in Word. The word count shows the length of the draft while you speak.

sections.heading: Privacy and the browser version
sections.body:
The Dictation tool uses your browser's speech recognition. Chrome may send the audio you speak to Google's speech service to turn it into text. Lazur does not receive that audio. Microsoft's Dictate uses its own service, and its help article describes what it does with your speech, so read that article before you dictate private documents.

If you dictate into more than one app, Lazur does this on a Mac: hold two keys, talk, and the text is typed into whatever app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

faq.a: Yes. Word has a Dictate feature for Microsoft 365 subscribers. It needs a microphone and a reliable internet connection. In Word for the web, select Dictate on the Home tab and speak.

faq.q: How do I turn on dictation in Word?
faq.a: Sign in with a Microsoft 365 account that includes Dictate, open your document, and select Dictate on the Home tab. Microsoft's help article has the steps for the web, desktop and phone versions, and notes that features can differ between them.

faq.q: Why can't I use Dictate in Word?
faq.a: Dictate is for Microsoft 365 subscribers, so check that you are signed in with a subscription account. You also need a working microphone and a reliable internet connection. If the button is still missing, try another version of Word.
